title: Cheeseburger on wheat bun with one medium patty

content.title: About
content.content: A cheeseburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a wheat bun, a single medium‑sized beef patty (about 100 g) and a slice of processed cheese. It is often topped with pickles, onions, ketchup and mustard. The combination of a soft bun, juicy patty and melted cheese makes it popular worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first cheeseburger was served in the United States in the 1920s.
A wheat bun gives a softer texture compared to the traditional sesame bun.
The cheese is usually processed to ensure even melting.
In some regions bacon is added, creating a bacon cheeseburger.
Cheeseburgers are a common item in speed‑eating competitions.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Processed cheese supplies calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Beef contains heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and cheese contain B12, B6, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Energy density
items.content: A cheeseburger provides a quick source of calories for active individuals.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: Because of the cheese, meat and bun, a cheeseburger can be calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Beef and processed cheese contain saturated fats, which may affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Ketchup, mustard and cheese add significant sodium, which can be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to dairy should avoid the cheese component.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the cheeseburger hot, splitting the bun and placing the patty with melted cheese inside. Add fresh vegetables, preferred sauces, and enjoy with fries or a side salad.

content.title: Storage
content.content: A freshly prepared cheeseburger is best eaten immediately. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours in an airtight container. Reheat in an oven or microwave to keep the bun from becoming soggy.
